From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Realtime stream — intermittent silence (region: us-west-2)

Adding findings from a quick run against Samira's logs:

- Observed repeated sequences where the WebSocket frame flow pauses and the client receives no DATA frames for 7–13s while the TCP connection stays ESTABLISHED.
- Server-side trace shows model output tokens were generated in the runtime, but the chunked transfer buffer on the frontend node did not flush during those windows.
- Root suspects: (1) socket_write backpressure under high concurrent KV-cache reads, (2) our chunked flusher thread being starved by GC pauses in the hot path (uncommon but plausible under this workload).

Mitigations to try ASAP:
1) Temporarily enable aggressive flush (force-send chunk every 100ms) on affected frontends.
2) Route ClearSight traffic to a more isolated pool (smaller shared-tenancy blast radius).
3) Short-term: enable client-side shorter idle timeout so clients reconnect rather than sit in silent state.

I can push a config toggle to us-west-2 that forces the flush behavior; it takes ~6–8 minutes to roll. Need approval to proceed.

— Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Update for exec brief & post-mortem notes: we rolled the aggressive flush toggle to the isolated pool at 12:22 PT and routed ClearSight traffic there by 12:30. Observed impact:

- Immediate reduction in silent windows: median silence dropped from ~9s -> ~0.9s across a 4-hour sample.
- Error rate (502/504) unchanged — indicates client was not timing out connections; problem was server-side chunk flush.
- CPU on isolated frontends increased ~6% but within headroom; memory GC patterns improved after flush fixes were deployed in the runtime bump (v2.8.3-roll).

Customer response: Samira reported normal UX restored by 13:10 PT. We should follow up with a formal RCA and offer a one-time credit for the billing spike window.

Next steps (owner):
- Rishi: schedule a capacity-hardening run and make the flush-health metrics permanent.
- Dev: open a runtime bug (JIRA-RT-9182) with stack traces and GC samples.
- Laura: send a short post-incident note to ClearSight with remediation steps and proposed credit.
- Aisha: decide on commercial goodwill (credit amount) and coordinate with Finance.

I'll attach the snapshot and the flusher metrics to the PMR.

— Marissa
